nearest_prs.read: Title, body and all review comments read this session: rest a manikin's cannulated forearm on a foam wedge, lifting it about the elbow and moving the looped IV line clear; voids on cannula-site force, cannula pull over 4.45 N, wrist bend or speed. Body does not mention a roller clamp.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shared context only: an IV line to a cannula on a forearm, with a pulled line as a harm condition. Its skill is lifting and placing a limb (patient handling); ours never touches the arm and is fine control of a 6 g clamp's wheel against 3 N while keeping the loose clamp from sliding along its line. Different object, different action, different success state (forearm on wedge vs wheel at its stop). The tug-the-line void is a common safety guard, not the task. Honest risk: a reviewer may group both as 'IV line care near a cannula'; the manipulated part and goal differ completely.

physical_skill: Roll a 12 mm wheel 22 mm against about 3 N of joint friction on a 6 g clamp lying loose on soft tubing, keeping the body from sliding along the line (by pressing it to the table through the wheel, or by holding its walls), without tugging the line to the cannula, then let go.
valid_shortcuts: GPU red team on this exact task.py (sha unchanged since): nothing 0; pinch tubing upstream and push wheel 0; careless push 0; stopped part way 0.4; hand left on wheel 0; tug patient line 0 (latched); lift and carry 0; drag while pressed 0; light touch 0. Valid solutions: one-handed press-and-roll (demo 1.0 twice) or two-handed hold-and-roll. Dream-1 this session: 0 (hovered beside the clamp, never rolled the wheel).
